spec.title: Summit
spec.subtitle: The stone that crowns the sky

chapters.label: CHAPTER 01 · NAMES OF THE PEAK
chapters.heading: A chorus of tongues rests on the ridge.
chapters.body: Mount Everest is known in Nepali as Sagarmāthā, meaning head in the sky, in Sherpa as Chamolangma, and in Tibetan as Jomolangma, lit. holy mother. The Chinese transcription Zhūmùlǎngmǎ Fēng mirrors the Tibetan name. The British survey named it after Sir George Everest despite his objections.

chapters.label: CHAPTER 02 · GEOMETRY OF GREATNESS
chapters.heading: Layers of ancient sea lie beneath the snow.
chapters.body: From summit to base the mountain comprises three formations. The upper Qomolangma Formation of Ordovician limestone holds microscopic crinoid fragments. Below, the Yellow Band of Cambrian marble shows a yellowish brown hue. The lower North Col Formation consists of schist, phyllite and marble, all thrust southward by low-angle faults.

heroImage.attribution: Luca Galuzzi (Lucag) · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

chapters.label: CHAPTER 03 · MEASURING THE SKY
chapters.heading: A joint survey fixed the final number.
chapters.body: The most recent joint survey by Nepalese and Chinese authorities in 2020 measured the summit at 8,848.86 m above sea level. This figure updates earlier estimates and confirms Everest as the highest point on Earth. The measurement reflects both modern technology and long-standing international cooperation.
